summary: Turtle can call your functions when the user clicks or presses a key. You register each function once, and turtle runs it every time that event happens.
notes: screen.onscreenclick(move_to_click) passes the function. Writing move_to_click() would call it once right away.
Key names are case-sensitive Tk names like "Left", "Up", "space", and "a".
screen.listen() is required for onkey(). Without it, key presses are ignored.
pitfall: Writing screen.onkey(move(-STEP, 0), "Left") calls move once at startup and registers None, so the Left key does nothing.
shot_note: After one click near the top left and three Right presses.
